answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to forge a costly, verifiable work history before it can earn. Instead of trusting a new identity at face value, peers check how long it has contributed useful, graded work and how much stake it would lose if it misbehaves. Like a gale that strips away loose sails, this test removes cheap copies: an attacker must repeat the whole expensive history for every fake identity, while a violet flag on one bad record warns the whole network and makes the next copy even harder to launch.
